compiled_state.title: DSO cross-session PR ownership: PreToolUse-enforced wrapper + Session-Id trailer + retro coverage
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Context
DSO sessions create PRs without any session-identifying marker. When a session resumes from auto-compact (memory loss) or another session encounters the PR, destructive PR-action code paths in merge-to-main-pr.sh, debug-everything, phase-10-merge-verify, and end-session resolve target PRs purely by current branch name. A post-compact session was observed classifying another session's PR as a "mystery" and attempting to close it. The Claude Code runtime sets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID per session (UUID); this epic stamps that as a Session-Id: trailer on the PR body at creation. Following the bot-psychologist R2 lesson from the prior epic (7510-0198) — load-bearing enforcement must be structural, not behavioral — the canonical action path becomes a single wrapper script pr-destructive-action.sh that internalizes the ownership check, AND a PreToolUse hook intercepts any bash invocation of "gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment)" that does not go through the wrapper. SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md instructions are framed as negative directives (prohibitions) pointing to the single permitted path, not as procedural "remember to invoke X before Y" composition that the prior epic's bot-psych review identified as behavioral-drift-prone.

## Success Criteria
- plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main-pr.sh stamps "Session-Id: $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID" and "Generated-By: dso-merge-to-main-pr.sh" trailers into the PR body at create; the value is shell-quote-sanitized before injection; shell unit test asserts both trailer lines are present and that a synthetic newline-containing session ID is rejected at sanitization with a clear error.
- New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-owned-by-session.sh <pr-number> calls gh pr view --json body, parses the Session-Id: trailer, compares to $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, and exits 0 (own), 1 (foreign), 2 (absent), 3 (api_error) with structured stderr identifying the case; shell unit test covers all 4 exits with synthetic fixtures; the helper itself never invokes gh pr <destructive>.
- New plugins/dso/scripts/pr-destructive-action.sh <pr-number> <action> [args...] is the single permitted path for destructive PR actions: it internally invokes pr-owned-by-session.sh, then on exit 0 executes gh pr <action> [args...], on exit 1/2/3 emits structured stderr with the case identifier and exits non-zero (fail-closed). Shell unit test covers all 4 internal-check outcomes end-to-end.
- New PreToolUse hook plugins/dso/hooks/check-pr-destructive-action.sh parses the Bash tool command string and blocks any invocation containing gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) that does not also contain pr-destructive-action.sh; hook integration test asserts the block fires on a direct "gh pr close N" invocation and does NOT fire on "pr-destructive-action.sh N close".
- CLAUDE.md "Never Do These" rule 25 (negative-directive form): "Never invoke gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly. Destructive PR actions go through pr-destructive-action.sh (the only permitted path). Direct invocations are blocked by PreToolUse hook check-pr-destructive-action.sh." Rule additionally documents the exit-code contract (0/1/2/3) and the rationale (session ownership; see fe66-f05b).
- All call sites in shell scripts that previously called gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) directly — merge-to-main-pr.sh:437/549/1295 — are migrated to invoke pr-destructive-action.sh. SKILL.md sites — debug-everything/SKILL.md:1175, phase-10-merge-verify.md:51, end-session/SKILL.md:242 — are rewritten as negative-directive instruction blocks naming pr-destructive-action.sh as the only permitted path; the rewrite is in addition to the PreToolUse hook (which is the load-bearing enforcement).
- CI test under plugins/dso/tests/ scans every .sh file under plugins/dso/ for gh pr (close|merge|edit|comment) invocations and fails the build when any such invocation appears outside pr-destructive-action.sh itself. SKILL.md files are explicitly excluded from this scan (false-positive surface — prose containing the script name in instruction text would pass meaninglessly per bot-psych analysis). Behavioral compliance on SKILL.md sites is enforced by the PreToolUse hook at runtime, not by the grep test.
- Two-session integration test: simulate session A with CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-A-uuid creating a synthetic PR (trailer stamped); switch to CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=session-B-uuid and attempt close/merge/comment via pr-destructive-action.sh — all three refused (exit 1, structured stderr). Positive case (session A acts on its own PR) succeeds. Edge case (PR with stripped trailer) returns exit 2 absent — included in the same test.
- Pre-existing un-trailered PRs migration: a one-shot script plugins/dso/scripts/backfill-pr-session-trailers.sh lists all currently-open PRs and, for each PR whose author matches the local "gh api /user --jq .login", prompts the operator to either (a) stamp this user's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID as the trailer retroactively or (b) skip. Script logs each decision; idempotent (skips PRs that already have a trailer). The migration is operator-driven, never automatic, never claims ownership for a session not actually the owner.
- CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID stability empirical verification (preplanning verification task before sprint dispatch): probe the env var value across (a) initial session start, (b) after one auto-compact event, (c) after a multi-day idle resume if reproducible. Record observed behavior in the epic ticket. If the variable is NOT stable across compaction (the critical Red Team scenario), this epic's primary mechanism is invalid — the verification task surfaces this before implementation work begins and the design is revised before sprint.

## Dependencies
None blocking.

Relates_to:
- 7510-0198 (DSO orphan story/task prevention) — same R2 structural-enforcement pattern; coordinate the new plugins/dso/tests/ CI grep test layout to share scanner harness
- 0777-0f3d (multi-agent coordination) — pr-owned-by-session.sh returns 0 for all agents sharing the same CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; document this explicitly
- 0cf2-42b5 (sprint SKILL.md refactor) — coordinate SKILL.md negative-directive injection with the refactor's phase layout
- 2239-1545 (cross-runtime harness adapter) — CI grep test targets .sh only, isolating runtime portability concerns to the hook implementation
- 70f6-05f1 (Clash parallel review) — Session-Id is immutable once stamped; document the ordering guarantee
- fb32-215c (workflow-config PR vs merge flag) — both PR creation paths (auto-merge mode and PR-only mode) must stamp the trailer

## Approach
Adopt the bot-psychologist R2 redesign in full. Single permitted invocation path via pr-destructive-action.sh wrapper that internalizes the ownership check. Load-bearing enforcement via PreToolUse hook that blocks any direct gh pr destructive invocation. CI grep test scopes to .sh files only (SKILL.md prose generates false positives). CLAUDE.md rule and SKILL.md instructions are negative-directive form ("never invoke gh pr X directly; use the wrapper"), not procedural composition. Sanitize CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID before injection. Distinct exit codes (0/1/2/3) for own/foreign/absent/api_error. Operator-driven backfill script handles pre-existing PRs. Preplanning verification task confirms CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID stability across compaction before sprint dispatch — if the variable is not stable, the design is revised before implementation.

## Scenario Analysis
- CRITICAL — CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID stability across compaction unverified — addressed by preplanning empirical verification task
- HIGH — CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID unset in non-Claude-Code contexts — addressed by fail-closed exit 2 (absent); operator-driven backfill provides manual escape hatch
- HIGH — Concurrent destructive actions in same session — same-session-actors-can-proceed is the intended behavior; advisory lock deferred to follow-on if observed
- HIGH — gh pr view fails or times out — addressed by distinct exit code 3 (api_error); fail-closed at the wrapper; stderr distinguishes from foreign/absent
- HIGH — Pre-existing PRs lack trailer — addressed by operator-driven backfill script, idempotent, owner-only
- HIGH — SKILL.md sites are prose, not shell code — addressed by R2 redesign — PreToolUse hook is load-bearing; CI grep test rescoped to .sh only; SKILL.md instructions are negative directives
- MEDIUM — PR body truncation drops trailer — trailer at end-of-body so truncation impact is detectable; helper exits 2 (absent) if approaching GitHub 65k limit at create, fail-closed
- MEDIUM — CI grep test fails on multi-line gh pr or wrappers — addressed by scoping to .sh only — wrappers scanned same as direct calls
- MEDIUM — Special chars in CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID — addressed by sanitization at injection time
- MEDIUM — No documented override for manual execution — addressed by operator-driven backfill script; CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID is the runtime contract for normal execution
- MEDIUM — gh pr view --json body may normalize/strip trailer — addressed by sanitization + unit test with synthetic GitHub-API-returned body fixtures
